players.product: competitive nuclear and gas generation supplying data-center load (ERCOT/PJM)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 RECORD RESULTS (CFO): Vistra delivered $5.912 billion in adjusted EBITDA for full year 2025 — $4.290 billion from generation and $1.622 billion from retail — and approximately $3.6 billion of adjusted free cash flow before growth, both meaningfully above the midpoint of the original guidance ranges. Generation benefited from the hedging program and 2 months of Lotus assets, more than offsetting extended outages at Martin Lake Unit 1 and the Moss Landing battery facilities. Retail's record was partly driven by non-repeating tailwinds; over the medium term retail is expected at approximately $1.4 billion of adjusted EBITDA.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA $5.912 billion (generation $4.290 billion, retail $1.622 billion); approximately $3.6 billion adjusted free cash flow before growth; retail medium-term approximately $1.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER LOAD TIMING (CEO): 'we continue to believe the impact of data centers on tightening supply-demand dynamics will not meaningfully begin until late 2027 or early 2028, given most build schedules and interconnect timing.' Vistra maintains its view that annual peak load growth of at least 3% to 5% in ERCOT and low single-digit growth in PJM is achievable through 2030, with overall load growth outpacing peak demand (higher utilization, not just short peaks). U.S. electricity consumption reached an all-time peak of approximately 4,200 terawatt hours in 2025, up about 2.5% versus 2024. Hyperscaler capital spending 'is expected to eclipse $700 billion in 2026, equivalent to roughly 50% year-over-year growth', which management cites as support for sustained load growth.
quarterly_data.figure: ERCOT peak load growth at least 3% to 5% and PJM low single-digit through 2030; data-center tightening from late 2027 or early 2028; hyperscaler capex expected to eclipse $700 billion in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: GAS FLEET SCALE-UP VIA M&A: in October 2025 Vistra closed the acquisition of 7 natural gas facilities totaling approximately 2,600 megawatts from Lotus Infrastructure Partners (PJM, New England, New York, California), and agreed to acquire Cogentrix Energy — 10 natural gas facilities totaling approximately 5,500 megawatts — at approximately $730 per kilowatt net of expected tax benefits, expected to close in the second half of 2026 with mid-single-digit adjusted FCF-before-growth per share accretion in 2027. After Cogentrix the combined-cycle fleet totals approximately 26 gigawatts, currently at a utilization rate of approximately 60%, which management expects higher energy demand to drive materially higher. During Winter Storm Fern's tightest hours thermal generation supplied approximately 93% of ERCOT power.
quarterly_data.figure: Lotus approximately 2,600 megawatts (closed); Cogentrix approximately 5,500 megawatts at approximately $730 per kilowatt; combined-cycle fleet approximately 26 gigawatts at approximately 60% utilization

quarterly_data.signal: NUCLEAR CONTRACTING: Vistra has now contracted approximately 3.8 gigawatts of nuclear capacity (including uprates) under long-term PPAs with Amazon Web Services (Comanche Peak) and Meta (PJM plants) — 'more than any other power company in the country.' It still sees an opportunity to contract up to an additional 3.2 gigawatts across Beaver Valley and Comanche Peak, including potential uprates of approximately 200 megawatts at Comanche Peak (the CFO says the 433 MW Meta uprates plus these 200 MW cover the uprate opportunity at existing plants). At full ramp of all nuclear agreements management sees a pathway to nearly 25% adjusted FCF-before-growth accretion annually; the PJM uprates need growth capital over an 8-year period, mostly after 2028. Beaver Valley draws 'a very high level of interest' for either colocation or a front-of-the-meter deal.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 3.8 gigawatts contracted; up to an additional 3.2 gigawatts available (Beaver Valley, Comanche Peak) incl. approximately 200 megawatts Comanche Peak uprate; nearly 25% FCF accretion at full ramp

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 UPLIFT FROM ANNOUNCED DEALS (CFO): 2026 guidance and the 2027 midpoint opportunity will be updated once Cogentrix closes (expected second half of 2026); from disclosed terms the Cogentrix and Meta transactions add 'in the neighborhood of $700 million to $750 million' to 2027, absent curve changes, with only one Meta asset contributing a full year in 2027 (the second contract begins in late 2027). Adjusted FCF before growth per share is seen above $12.5 for 2026, approximately $16 including Cogentrix, the Meta operating PPAs and a simplifying buyback assumption, and in the range of $22 to $25 if all 2026-2030 cash available were used for buybacks.
quarterly_data.figure: Cogentrix + Meta add $700 million to $750 million to 2027; FCF/share above $12.5 (2026), approximately $16 with announced deals, $22 to $25 illustrative

quarterly_data.signal: CAPITAL ALLOCATION (CFO): more than $10 billion of cash expected through year-end 2027; after approximately $3 billion to equity holders (buybacks plus common and preferred dividends) and approximately $4 billion to growth (Cogentrix, the Permian gas units, the Meta-backed PJM nuclear uprates), more than $3 billion of additional capital remains available, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA of approximately 2.3x by year-end 2027. About $1.8 billion of buyback authorization remains; approximately 167 million shares retired since November 2021 at an average cost below $36. Return threshold remains mid-teens or higher levered. Nearly half of total adjusted EBITDA is expected to come from highly stable sources (contracts plus retail).
quarterly_data.figure: more than $10 billion cash through year-end 2027; approximately $4 billion growth; more than $3 billion unallocated; approximately 2.3x leverage; $1.8 billion buyback authorization

quarterly_data.signal: NEW-BUILD PIPELINE AND EQUIPMENT (Stacey Dore): between capacity already added and what is underway — the 433 megawatts of nuclear uprates, coal-to-gas conversions at Miami Fort and Coleto Creek, and the Permian gas plants in West Texas — 'it's over 3,600 megawatts of capacity.' The 500 megawatts of ERCOT gas augmentations are largely complete; PJM fleet augmentations under study could total approximately 300 megawatts. 'We do not see equipment or EPC as the gating items to building new generation', citing long-standing relationships with all turbine OEMs, ample access to high-voltage equipment, and third parties marketing already-purchased turbines. Management expects hyperscalers to contract new gas build, with customers ultimately taking gas risk under a large fixed capacity payment plus variable component; 2026 is 'the year in which customers are focusing on what is real and what is credible.'
quarterly_data.figure: over 3,600 megawatts added or underway; 500 megawatts ERCOT augmentations largely complete; approximately 300 megawatts PJM augmentations under study

connects_to.relationship: long-term power purchase agreement - carbon-free nuclear power from Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant supplied to AWS

contracts.signal: 20-year contract with Amazon at Comanche Peak: Amazon will site a facility on Vistra's property to use the 1,200 megawatts of capacity and plans to bring one-for-one backup generation. Initial energization is still expected in the fourth quarter of 2027 with full ramp by the fourth quarter of 2032; the agreement includes options to explore new nuclear development (uprates and small modular reactors), and management says the Comanche Peak uprate could potentially be added with the same customer. Separately, Vistra executed the Oak Hill solar PPA with Amazon.
contracts.type: 20-year nuclear PPA (co-located data center) — energization Q4 2027, full ramp Q4 2032

connects_to.relationship: long-term power purchase agreements at Vistra's PJM nuclear sites

contracts.signal: 20-year agreements with Meta announced in January 2026 cover 2,176 megawatts of operating capacity from Perry and Davis-Besse and an additional 433 megawatts of uprate capacity at Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley. Delivery of operating capacity is expected to start at Perry in December of 2026 and Davis-Besse in December 2027; Perry uprates are expected online in the fourth quarter of 2031, with one more uprate each year until all 4 are complete by the fourth quarter of 2034. Management says it is 'more akin to a typical front-of-the-meter deal', not tied to colocation or any particular load, and does not believe current PJM activity affects it; the operating-capacity PPAs need no additional spend.
contracts.type: 20-year nuclear PPA (front-of-the-meter) — Perry Dec 2026, Davis-Besse Dec 2027, uprates Q4 2031 to Q4 2034

connects_to.relationship: power purchase agreement - Pulaski renewable (solar) PPA

contracts.signal: Stacey Dore: 'We've executed on the Oak Hill solar PPA last year with Amazon as well as Pulaski with Microsoft. So we have those existing customer relationships.' CEO Jim Burke lists Pulaski among Vistra's 'contracted renewables such as Oak Hill and Pulaski'.
